claim_summary: FactorMAD contributes a feedback-driven, two-agent debate controller and a code-based factor development pipeline for interpretable stock-return prediction, with downstream portfolio simulations.

claim_evidence.quote:
The evaluation results are recorded and used as valuable feedback for the debating agents, informing their subsequent factor
proposals and critiques, thereby forming a closed-loop system that
enables iterative factor improvement.

As illustrated in Figure 2, our pipeline
consists of four key stages: generation, validation, correction, and
evaluation.

modules.name: Feedback-driven factor debate
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK matches first: agents propose and critique stock alpha factors using their predictive metrics, factor histories and factor-design requirements. Changing the task family requires redesigning the proposed artifacts, objective and feedback; this is not a task-neutral temporal utility. Initialization, seed selection and transcript retention support this single debate mechanism.

notes: No LLM training is contributed: GPT-4o is used as the base model. The factor development pipeline is counted as one integrated mechanism; its temporal checks are not promoted to a separate reusable GTS module. Standard predictive models, market data and TopK portfolio simulation are evaluation components, not additional contributed modules. Work-level decision_support records the portfolio application; the contributed modules directly implement forecasting_prediction. Process-validity mechanisms are described, but execution/repair success or failure measurements are not reported. Temporal validity records chronological splitting, not a demonstrated absence of every form of leakage.
